source: This loss of H3 density during differentiation was abolished by Pask knockdown (Figure 7B, Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by total H3 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion at the Myog upstream enhancer is not impaired by Pask knockdown, nor is the appearance of H3K27ac.
source: However, unlike the proximal Myog promoter, H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion at the Myog upstream enhancer is not impaired by Pask knockdown, nor is the appearance of H3K27ac (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MyoD recruitment to the Myog enhancer during differentiation is impaired by Pask knockdown, possibly due to the interdependence of the enhancer and promoter for optimal activation.
source: Interestingly, MyoD recruitment to the enhancer during differentiation is impaired similarly to the proximal promoter by Pask knockdown, possibly due to the interdependence of the enhancer and promoter for optimal activation (Sanyal et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and citation to prior work (Sanyal et al., 2012), with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The Mybph and Acta1 promoters, but not Myod, undergo H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion during differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts and this is Pask-dependent.
source: Like Myog, the Mybph and Acta1 promoters, but not Myod were reported to undergo H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion during differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts (Cheng et al., 2014) and this is also Pask-dependent (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-D and citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claim: Silencing of Mll3 at the onset of differentiation rescues the impaired Myog expression upon Pask knockdown.
source: If the enhanced H3K4me1 occupancy at the Myog promoter is responsible for the transcriptional repression observed upon loss of Pask activity, then silencing of Mll3 at the onset of differentiation, which is specific for deposition of H3K4me1 marks might rescue the expression of Myog upon Pask knockdown. Indeed, we found that Mll3 knockdown in Pask-siRNA cells rescued the impaired Myog expression and restored differentiation as indicated by the Mylpf expression (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Mll3 knockdown in Pask-siRNA cells restores differentiation as indicated by Mylpf expression.
source: Indeed, we found that Mll3 knockdown in Pask-siRNA cells rescued the impaired Myog expression and restored differentiation as indicated by the Mylpf expression (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Pask is an essential mediator whereby differentiation cues stimulate H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion and chromatin remodeling to facilitate MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter.
source: Taken together, our results show that Pask is an essential mediator whereby differentiation cues stimulate H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion and chromatin remodeling to facilitate MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter.
evidence: This claim is a summary inference from all the ChIP data showing Pask effects on histone marks and MyoD recruitment.

claim: The requirement of Pask for loss of H3K4me1 and total H3 from the Myog promoter is related to Wdr5 phosphorylation since Wdr5S49E expression is sufficient to deplete H3K4me1 marks and total H3 occupancy on the Myog promoter even in the absence of differentiation cues.
source: The requirement of Pask for loss of H3K4me1 and total H3 from the Myog promoter appears to be related to Wdr5 phosphorylation since Wdr5S49E expression was sufficient to deplete H3K4me1 marks (Figure 7D) and total H3 occupancy (Figure 7E) on the Myog promoter even in the absence of differentiation cues.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: The depletion of H3K4me1 and total H3 at Day 1 of differentiation is prevented by the expression of Wdr5S49A.
source: In contrast, the depletion of H3K4me1 and total H3 at Day 1 of differentiation was prevented by the expression of Wdr5S49A (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: The effects of Wdr5S49A and Wdr5S49E expression on H3K4me1 and total H3 mirror those on MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter.
source: These effects of Wdr5S49A and Wdr5S49E expression mirror those on MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter (Figure 6G).
evidence: This claim is an inference connecting the histone mark data with the MyoD recruitment data.

claim: Wdr5 phosphorylation status dictates MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter, perhaps via H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion.
source: Thus, Wdr5 phosphorylation status appears to dictate MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter, perhaps via H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion.
evidence: This claim is a speculative inference about the mechanism linking Wdr5 phosphorylation to MyoD recruitment.

claim: Pask-/- mice are developmentally normal despite the role of Pask in muscle regeneration response to injury in vivo.
source: In spite of the role of Pask in the muscle regeneration response to injury in vivo that we have described, Pask-/- mice are developmentally normal.
evidence: This claim is based on observation of the Pask-/- mouse phenotype.

claim: The normal development of Pask-/- mice is similar to the phenotype of mice lacking the key myogenic transcription factors, Myod, Pax7, Myf5 or Mrf4.
source: While surprising, this is similar to the phenotype of mice lacking the key myogenic transcription factors, Myod (Rudnicki et al., 1992), Pax7 (Seale et al., 2000), Myf5 (Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2004; Kaul et al., 2000) or Mrf4 (Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2004) (reviewed in (Musarò and 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on myogenic transcription factor knockouts.

claim: Myoblasts from Pask-/- mice have acquired resistance to Pask inhibitor-mediated suppression of myocyte differentiation, indicating that constitutive knockout results in a pro-differentiation compensatory response that is Pask-independent.
source: Moreover, we found that myoblasts from Pask-/- mice had acquired resistance to Pask inhibitor-mediated suppression of myocyte differentiation, indicating that constitutive knockout results in a pro-differentiation compensatory response that is Pask-independent.
evidence: This claim is supported by the observation that BioE-1197 has no effect on Pask-/- myoblasts (Figure 1F-G).

claim: Pask-siRNA or PASK-inhibited cells exhibit modest induction of Myog, its target genes and H3K4me3 abundance upon differentiation, suggesting the presence of Pask-independent mechanisms to drive myogenin induction.
source: Similarly, Pask-siRNA or PASK-inhibited cells typically exhibited modest induction of Myog, its target genes and H3K4me3 abundance upon differentiation, suggesting the presence of Pask-independent mechanisms to drive myogenin induction.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that differentiation is impaired but not completely abolished by Pask loss.

claim: Myf5 and other transcriptional regulators may drive some of the Pask-independent activation of the Myog promoter, as Pask-/- myoblasts exhibit elevated expression of Myf5.
source: It's noteworthy that Pask-/- myoblasts exhibit elevated expression of Myf5 (Figure 2B), which has been shown to be able to compensate for the loss of MyoD function (Conerly et al., 2016; Rudnicki et al., 1992). Thus, it is possible that Myf5 and other transcriptional regulators drive some of the Pask-independent activation of the Myog promoter.
evidence: This claim is speculative inference based on elevated Myf5 in Pask-/- cells and prior work showing Myf5 can compensate for MyoD.

claim: The Pask-Wdr5 signaling axis is necessary and sufficient for full activation of the Myog promoter and subsequent myoblast fusion.
source: Nonetheless, our data demonstrate that the Pask-Wdr5 signaling axis is necessary and sufficient for full activation of the Myog promoter and subsequent myoblast fusion.
evidence: This claim is a summary of the experimental findings showing Pask-Wdr5 effects on Myog expression and differentiation.

claim: Pask expression is high in stem and progenitor cell types.
source: We have shown that Pask expression is high in stem and progenitor cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: In ES cells, the Pask promoter is occupied by the pluripotency promoting transcription factors, Oct4 and Nanog.
source: In ES cells, the Pask promoter is occupied by the pluripotency promoting transcription factors, Oct4 and Nanog (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Oct4 and Nanog transcription factor occupancy of the Pask promoter coincides with Pask transcriptional activation as indicated by the occupancy of RNA PolII as well as the activating H3K4me3 and H3K27ac chromatin modifications.
source: This transcription factor occupancy coincided with the Pask transcriptional activation as indicated by the occupancy of RNA PolII as well as the activating H3K4me3 and H3K27ac chromatin modifications.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: During muscle regeneration in vivo, Pask expression is dramatically induced as early as 3 days after injury, coincident with expansion of the satellite cell population and stimulation of MyoG expression.
source: During muscle regeneration in vivo expression is dramatically induced as early as 3 days after injury (Figure 1H), coincident with expansion of the satellite cell population and stimulation of MyoG expression (Braun and Gautel, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1H and citation to prior work (Braun and Gautel, 2011).

claim: MyoG and MyoD bind the Pask promoter.
source: We showed that MyoG and MyoD bind the Pask promoter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B), which is marked by broad domains of H3K4me3 occupancy similar to those found in other lineage-specifying genes (Benayoun et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-B.

claim: The Pask promoter is marked by broad domains of H3K4me3 occupancy similar to those found in other lineage-specifying genes.
source: We showed that MyoG and MyoD bind the Pask promoter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B), which is marked by broad domains of H3K4me3 occupancy similar to those found in other lineage-specifying genes (Benayoun et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data and citation to prior work (Benayoun et al., 2014).

claim: Terminal differentiation of ES cells and C2C12 myoblasts results in a decline in Pask expression, which ultimately reaches a low steady-state abundance when differentiation is complete.
source: Terminal differentiation of ES cells and C2C12 myoblasts results in a decline in Pask expression, which ultimately reaches a low steady-state abundance when differentiation is complete.
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data from differentiation time courses.

claim: The pattern of Pask expression is consistent with the expression of other key regulators of terminal differentiation like MyoD and hints at the importance of Pask in the lineage commitment process.
source: This pattern is consistent with the expression of other key regulators of terminal differentiation like MyoD and hints at the importance of Pask in the lineage commitment process.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the expression pattern of Pask.

claim: Pharmacologic inhibition of Pask activity causes a loss of terminal differentiation in ES cells to a neuronal fate, C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells to adipocytes and C2C12 myoblasts to myotubes.
source: Pharmacologic inhibition of Pask activity caused a loss of terminal differentiation in three differentiation paradigms: ES cells to a neuronal fate, C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells to adipocytes and C2C12 myoblasts to myotubes.
evidence: This claim is a summary of the differentiation experiments across multiple cell types.

claim: Wdr5 has been previously implicated in controlling stem cell maintenance, with Oct4 associating with Wdr5 and recruiting H3K4me3 complexes to its target promoters to induce transcriptional activation and maintenance of pluripotency.
source: Wdr5 has been previously implicated in controlling stem cell maintenance. For example, Oct4 associates with Wdr5 and recruits H3K4me3 complexes to its target promoters to induce transcriptional activation and maintenance of pluripotency (Ang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Ang et al., 2011).

claim: In C2C12 myoblasts, Wdr5 interacts with Pax7 to enforce myogenic specification.
source: In C2C12 myoblasts, Wdr5 was shown to interact with Pax7 to enforce myogenic specification (Kawabe et al., 2012; McKinnell et al., 2008; Rudnicki et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Kawabe et al., 2012; McKinnell et al., 2008; Rudnicki et al., 2008).

claim: The results provide a new regulatory role for Wdr5 in promoting differentiation via the expression of key target genes.
source: Our results provide a new regulatory role for Wdr5 in promoting differentiation via the expression of key target genes.
evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the experimental findings.

claim: The results define a novel regulatory paradigm wherein the function of Wdr5 is modulated by Pask-dependent phosphorylation.
source: More importantly, these results define a novel regulatory paradigm wherein the function of Wdr5 is modulated by Pask-dependent phosphorylation.
evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the experimental findings showing Pask phosphorylates Wdr5 to regulate its function.

claim: It is likely, but remains to be established, whether Wdr5 phosphorylation is a conserved and required mechanism whereby Pask promotes the differentiation of other stem and progenitor cells.
source: While we deem it likely, it remains to be established whether Wdr5 phosphorylation is a conserved and required mechanism whereby Pask promotes the differentiation of other stem and progenitor cells.
evidence: This claim is speculation about the generalizability of the findings.

claim: Differentiation cues engage and activate the signaling pathways and transcriptional networks that combine to drive terminal differentiation.
source: Differentiation cues engage and activate the signaling pathways and transcriptional networks that combine to drive terminal differentiation (Basson, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Basson, 2012) and represents established knowledge.

claim: While a pioneering transcription factor like MyoD can occupy its target promoters in a sequence-specific manner, the full activation of the MyoD transcriptional response depends upon signaling from differentiation cues.
source: While a pioneering transcription factor like MyoD can occupy its target promoters in a sequence-specific manner, the full activation of the MyoD transcriptional response depends upon signaling from differentiation cues (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005).

claim: Differentiation cues are thought to enhance MyoD binding to its target promoters and recruit histone modifying proteins to initiate the expression of differentiation genes.
source: These cues, including those used in vitro treatment with insulin, are thought to enhance MyoD binding to its target promoters and recruit histone modifying proteins to initiate the expression of differentiation genes (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005; Blum and Dynlacht, 2013; Braun and Gautel, 2011; Dilworth and Blais, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005; Blum and Dynlacht, 2013; Braun and Gautel, 2011; Dilworth and Blais, 2011).

claim: Ectopic expression of Pask or phospho-mimetic Wdr5 is sufficient to induce MyoD binding to target promoters, recruitment of histone modifying proteins, and myogenic gene expression in the absence of differentiation cues.
source: Ectopic expression of Pask or phospho-mimetic Wdr5 was sufficient to induce all of these effects in the absence of differentiation cues (Figure 2K–J, Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2K-J and 5H.

claim: Pask might be a critical node in the signaling network connecting differentiation cues with myogenic gene expression.
source: These data raise the possibility that Pask might be a critical node in the signaling network connecting differentiation cues with myogenic gene expression.
evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the sufficiency of Pask to induce differentiation.

claim: Pask activity and the Pask-Wdr5 interaction are stimulated by differentiation cues.
source: Consistent with that hypothesis, we found that Pask activity was stimulated by differentiation cues as was the Pask-Wdr5 interaction (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinase assay and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4F and 4A.

claim: Differentiation cues act, at least in part, to drive the myogenic transcriptional program via Pask activation and phosphorylation of Wdr5.
source: We therefore believe that differentiation cues act, at least in part, to drive the myogenic transcriptional program via Pask activation and phosphorylation of Wdr5.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the data showing Pask is activated by differentiation cues and phosphorylates Wdr5 to promote differentiation.

claim: It remains unknown how Pask activity and the Pask-Wdr5 interaction are stimulated by differentiation cues.
source: It remains unknown how Pask activity and the Pask-Wdr5 interaction are stimulated by differentiation cues, but we suggest that these phenomena are likely central components of this signaling pathway.
evidence: This claim acknowledges a gap in knowledge while speculating about importance.

claim: H3K4me1 was recently demonstrated to be a transcriptionally repressive mark at the promoters of myogenic genes.
source: H3K4me1 was recently demonstrated to be a transcriptionally repressive mark at the promoters of myogenic genes (Cheng et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claim: In response to differentiation cues, H3K4me1 is further methylated to H3K4me3 on myogenic promoters to initiate their expression.
source: In response to differentiation cues, H3K4me1 is further methylated to H3K4me3 on these promoters to initiate their expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claim: H3K4 monomethylation is catalyzed by the Wdr5-containing Mll3/Mll4 complexes.
source: H3K4 monomethylation is catalyzed by the Wdr5-containing Mll3/Mll4 complexes (Hu et al., 2013), while the Wdr5-containing Mll1/Mll2 complexes catalyze H3K4 trimethylation (Shilatifard, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Hu et al., 2013; Shilatifard, 2012).

claim: The Wdr5-containing Mll1/Mll2 complexes catalyze H3K4 trimethylation.
source: H3K4 monomethylation is catalyzed by the Wdr5-containing Mll3/Mll4 complexes (Hu et al., 2013), while the Wdr5-containing Mll1/Mll2 complexes catalyze H3K4 trimethylation (Shilatifard, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Shilatifard, 2012).

claim: It has been predicted that differentiation cues promote a Mll3/Mll4 to Mll1/Mll2 switch on myogenic promoters via an unknown mechanism.
source: Thus, it has been predicted that differentiation cues promote a Mll3/Mll4 to Mll1/Mll2 switch on myogenic promoters via an unknown mechanism (Cheng et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claim: Pask phosphorylation of Wdr5 might be required for the Mll3/Mll4 to Mll1/Mll2 switch on myogenic promoters.
source: We speculate that Pask phosphorylation of Wdr5 might be required for this process.
evidence: This claim is speculation based on the data showing Pask-Wdr5 effects on H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion.

claim: Pask silencing prevents the H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion on the Myog promoter in response to differentiation cues and silencing of Mll3 rescues the defect in the induction of Myog expression caused by Pask silencing.
source: For example, Pask silencing prevented the H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion on the Myog promoter in response to differentiation cues and silencing of Mll3 rescued the defect in the induction of Myog expression caused by Pask silencing.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 7A-B and 7C.

claim: H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 are unaffected at the Myod promoter or at the Myod and Myog enhancers during differentiation in Pask-silenced condition.
source: Interestingly, H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 was unaffected at the Myod promoter or at the Myod and Myog enhancers during differentiation in Pask-silenced condition.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Pask and Wdr5 phosphorylation are not required for the enzymatic activity of the Mll1/2 or Mll3/4 complexes, but only for their activity on specific promoters like Myog, Acta1 and Mybph.
source: This suggests that Pask and Wdr5 phosphorylation are not required for the enzymatic activity of the Mll1/2 or Mll3/4 complexes, but only for their activity on specific promoters like Myog, Acta1 and Mybph.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the selective effects of Pask on certain promoters but not others.

claim: The Myog, Acta1 and Mybph promoters are repressed during proliferation and required to be derepressed at the onset of differentiation.
